title: Universal photon blockade via two-photon light-matter interaction at chiral exceptional points
authors: Hai-Tao Dong, Meng-Long Song, Si-Yu Zhang, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, Dong Wang
abstract: The photon blockade (PB) effect is a hallmark non-classical phenomenon in quantum optics and finds important applications for building quantum sources, while the control of PB by the non-Hermitian exceptional points remains largely unexplored. In this work, we theoretically investigate universal photon blockade in a microcavity harboring chiral exceptional points (CEPs) for building multiplexing quantum sources with nonreciprocal photon statistics. The results reveal that the presence of the CEPs leads to a stark contrast in the photon statistics of two whispering-gallery modes with opposite propagating directions. That is, one mode exhibits a strong PB effect while the other displays either sub-Poissonian or super-Poissonian distribution. Our findings thus may pave the way for advanced applications of photon blockade, and provide a theoretical foundation for the selective generation of single-photon and two-photon emission
summary: The paper theoretically investigates how chiral exceptional points in an optical microcavity can be exploited to achieve universal photon blockade. By analyzing the system's nonreciprocal dynamics, the authors demonstrate that one direction of light propagation exhibits strong anti-bunching (PB), while the other shows different statistics. This provides a pathway for designing highly directional quantum sources.
main_problem: The study investigates achieving universal photon blockade (PB) using two-photon light-matter interactions within a microcavity system exhibiting chiral exceptional points (CEPs). The goal is to build multiplexing quantum sources with nonreciprocal photon statistics.
main_result: The presence of CEPs causes a stark contrast in photon statistics between the two counter-propagating modes: one mode exhibits strong PB ($g^{(2)} 	o 0$), while the other shows Poissonian or super-Poissonian distribution, enabling directional control.
method: Theoretical analysis using the extended cascade quantum master equation and deriving equations of motion for probability amplitudes. Photon statistics are diagnosed via equal-time second-order correlation functions, $g^{(2)}(0)$.
model_or_system: The system is an optical microcavity coupled to a quantum emitter (QE), modeled by a two-photon two-mode JC Hamiltonian ($H_{JC}$). The dynamics are governed by the master equation incorporating cavity and atomic decay rates.
key_observables: Second-order correlation functions ($g^{(2)}_L(0)$ and $g^{(2)}_R(0)$), mean photon numbers ($n_L, n_R$), and probability amplitudes of Fock states.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($g/\kappa$), detuning ($\Delta_c/\kappa$), phase ($\phi$), and cavity/mirror reflectivity ($r$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the weak-driving regime approximation in some sections, and the system dynamics are modeled using a master equation approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $g^{(2)}(0)$ dependence on parameters like coupling strength, phase, and detuning. Key findings show PB ($g^{(2)} 	o 0$) appearing selectively in one mode (e.g., the right cavity) under specific parameter settings ($\phi=0$ or $\Delta_c=0$).
paper_structure: The paper develops by first establishing the theoretical framework using a two-photon JC model and master equation dynamics. It then analyzes the system's steady-state behavior, focusing on how CEPs induce directional differences in photon statistics (PB vs. bunching) under varying driving conditions (resonant vs. detuned).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it explores non-Hermitian effects (CEPs) to engineer fundamental quantum phenomena like single-photon emission with unprecedented directional control, moving beyond standard cavity QED setups.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematics of the cavity QED systems and the equivalent models. (a) A standard resonator supporting degenerate CW and CCW modes. A two-level atom couples to both modes with equal strength g. κ denotes the cavity-waveguide decay rate. (b) A mirror on the waveguide introduces strong unidirectional coupling from the CCW to the CW mode, driving the system to CEPs. (c) The EP system is unfolded via mirror symmetry into a cascaded model with a spatial separation L. Ωc (Ωa) represents the driving strength of the pump field, and ωd (ωL) represents the driving frequency.

FIG. 3. Density plots of the steady-state equal-time second-order correlation functions versus the nonlinear atom-cavity coupling strength g/κ and the mirror reflectivity r under cavity driving. The system parameters are chosen as γ/κ = 1, Ωc/κ = 0.01, ∆a = 0, and φ = 0 and the white dashed line in the figure corresponds to the relation: g/κ = |2r −1| p
